katas.title: PTO save: reserve the new request against every active request, approved ones included
katas.findingRef: nethris extended course ch. 09 "Approved hours are not reserved again" (astraupskill/advanced/extended-course/09-reservations-and-balance-accounting.md:13)

seededDefectKey.scenario: Erin had 40h, an 8h request was approved (stored balance now 32). She requests 30h for November.
seededDefectKey.consequence: The approved 8h was already subtracted from PtoBalanceHours at final approval, and the patch subtracts it again: 8 + 30 > 32 is refused with "Insufficient balance" although she has 32h available. Every approved request permanently shrinks what an employee can request by its hours a second time.
Final approval deducts from the stored balance; only still-PENDING requests are reservations against it, which is why the original sums the Pending(...) subset.
Approved requests are loaded on purpose — for the date-overlap rule. Reusing the whole set for the balance sum conflates "occupies dates" with "still reserves hours".

katas.title: PTO decisions: the different-reviewer rule should only stop a second HR-stage decision by the same person
katas.findingRef: nethris extended course ch. 10, different final reviewer (astraupskill/advanced/extended-course/10-approval-workflows-and-authority.md:7)

seededDefectKey.scenario: Morgan holds the HR role and is also Erin's direct manager. Morgan approves the manager stage, then opens the same request again at the HR stage.
seededDefectKey.consequence: An "Hr" approval can never exist while the request is still PendingHr (the HR decision closes it), so the narrowed check is always false: one person now approves both stages and the balance is deducted with no second reviewer. The two-stage workflow silently becomes single-approver for every HR-role manager.

seededDefectKey.scenario: The rule the message still promises.
seededDefectKey.consequence: The guard exists to enforce a DIFFERENT final reviewer across stages; the patch keeps the message but drops the cross-stage comparison.
"They cannot then make the final HR decision on the same request under the different-reviewer rule" — approval history from ANY stage is part of the predicate.
